resolutions.researcher_notes: EIA's 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' table (opened as xlsx, parsed with openpyxl -- not a text-searchable web page, so confirmed by direct spreadsheet read) lists a row: Project Name 'East-West Project', Pipeline Operator Name 'Florida Gas Trans Co', State(s) 'LA,TX', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2019-01-22, Year In Service Date 2019, Docket Number 'CP17-8', Authority 'FERC' -- i.e. the project was built and placed in commercial service, matching Status=operating. Kinder Morgan's own FGT asset page (live URL now 404s -- confirmed dead, so citing the archived capture only) describes FGT in present tense as 'an approximately 5,300-mile system that transports natural gas from south Texas to south Florida,' i.e. an active, operating pipeline system that this in-service 2019 segment is part of. Two independent publishers (US EIA/FERC data and Kinder Morgan, the then-co-owner/operator) agree.

EIA's table is titled 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' and carries the East-West Project under it. Kinder Morgan's FGT page: FGT 'transports natural gas from south Texas to south Florida.' Texas Energy Report (archived; live URL now 200s to a login/'My Profile' page rather than the article -- adding the Wayback capture, which serves the full article, alongside): 'Florida Gas Transmission LLC (FGT) got the go-ahead for a portion of the 275 MMcf/d ... project' -- an FGT natural-gas transmission project. Three distinct publishers agree it is a gas pipeline.

EIA's 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' table row for 'East-West Project' (Florida Gas Trans Co, Docket CP17-8) shows Completed Date 2019-01-22, i.e. construction completed in 2019, matching the sheet's ConstructionYear=2019. Only one source states the specific completion year explicitly (Texas Energy Report's Aug. 2018 article predates completion and only reports a construction go-ahead, not a finish year), so single-source/medium.
Same EIA row: 'Year In Service Date': 2019 for the East-West Project, matching StartYear1=2019. Single source for the specific year (see Construction [ref] note); medium tier.

EIA table: 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)': 275 for East-West Project -- exact match. Texas Energy Report (archived): FGT 'got the go-ahead for a portion of the 275 MMcf/d ... project.' Pipeline News (Oct. 2018 issue, PDF, extracted with pdftotext -- text layer confirmed): FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION entry for 'East-West Project' lists 'Capacity: 275 MMDth/d.' MMDth/d and MMcf/d are used interchangeably for pipeline-quality natural gas capacity reporting (per the standing prose/unit-equivalence rule); all three publishers agree on the number 275. Three distinct publishers -> high/independent.

EIA's post-completion table row: 'Miles': 24.7 for East-West Project -- exact match to sheet's 24.70 mi. NOTE (not a CONCERN): Pipeline News' pre-construction entry (rev 6/18, i.e. before the Jan. 2019 completion) gives a planning-stage estimate of 'Length: 20 miles' for the same project -- a normal as-planned-vs-as-built variance, not a data problem; EIA's figure is the authoritative post-completion number and is the one that matches the sheet. Only one source (EIA) carries the final 24.7 mi figure, so medium/single-source.

Pipeline News (Oct. 2018, FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION -- REV 6/18 entry) lists 'Diameter: 12 inches' for the East-West Project, an exact match to the sheet's Diameter=12in. Confirmed by extracting the PDF's text layer with pdftotext -layout. Single source -> medium.

Pipeline News: 'Location: Matagorda and Wharton counties, TX; Acadia Parish, LA' for the East-West Project -- matches the sheet's StartPrefecture/District 'Matagorda County', Texas, ending in Louisiana. EIA's table corroborates at the state level only ('State(s)': 'LA,TX', Beg_State LA, End_State TX). Only one source (Pipeline News) states the county-level detail that is the sheet's primary_value, so medium; EIA is state-level corroboration.

EIA table: 'Cost (millions)': 68.9 for East-West Project. Texas Energy Report (archived): 'The overall project is expected to cost about $69 million.' Two distinct publishers agree closely (68.9M rounds to $69M, matching sheet's 69,000,000 USD).

Kinder Morgan's FGT asset page (archived; live page now 404s): 'FGT is owned by Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC, a 100 percent owned subsidiary of Citrus Corp' -- directly matches the sheet's Owner1='Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC', Owner1%=100.00%. EIA's table independently lists 'Pipeline Operator Name': 'Florida Gas Trans Co' for this project. Two distinct publishers.
